Summary: Project management and study operating model
Description:
As a solo learner, I want a realistic agile board and backlog so that I can practice delivery rituals while studying GCP data engineering.

Acceptance Criteria: Jira workspace, workflow, labels, fields, and import process are ready.

As a developer, I want GitHub and VS Code configured so that all learning work happens from a professional dev environment.

Acceptance Criteria: Repo cloned/opened in VS Code, Git identity configured, terminal workflow validated.

Summary: GCP first-time setup and cost guardrails
Description:
As a cloud learner, I want a controlled GCP project so that I can practice safely on free credits and avoid surprise costs.

Acceptance Criteria: Project, billing, APIs, IAM, budget alerts, and cleanup routine are documented.

As a data engineer, I want generated CSV and JSON datasets so that I can build a full medallion pipeline without external data dependencies.

Acceptance Criteria: Generated local data includes customers, products, orders, order_items, payments, shipments, and clickstream events.

Summary: Bronze raw landing zone in GCS
Description:
As a data engineer, I want raw immutable files in GCS so that the lake has a traceable source-of-record layer.

Acceptance Criteria: CSV and JSON files are uploaded to date-partitioned bronze paths with a manifest.

As a Spark learner, I want Dataproc reachable from VS Code over SSH so that I can develop and run Spark jobs remotely.

Acceptance Criteria: Single-node Dataproc cluster is created, SSH works, Spark UI is reachable, and repo is available on the cluster.

As a data engineer, I want bronze data converted to clean Parquet tables so that downstream processing is reliable and typed.

Acceptance Criteria: Silver jobs validate schemas, deduplicate, normalize timestamps, and write partitioned Parquet.

As an analyst, I want curated BigQuery marts so that sales, fulfillment, and customer metrics are queryable.

Acceptance Criteria: Gold fact/dimension tables and aggregate marts are available in BigQuery with validation queries.

As an operator, I want the pipeline scheduled and observable so that medallion jobs can be run end to end.

Acceptance Criteria: Composer DAG runs bronze checks, silver Spark jobs, gold loads, and validation tasks.

As a responsible learner, I want checks, notes, and cleanup steps so that the project is repeatable and low-cost.

Acceptance Criteria: Runbook, tests, screenshots checklist, and cleanup commands are complete.

Sign up or sign in to Atlassian, create a Jira project named GCP Medallion Learning, and choose a Scrum or Kanban template.

Detailed Steps: Open Atlassian, create Jira Free project, set project key GCPDE, confirm backlog and board are visible.

Acceptance Criteria: Project exists and can accept imported tasks.

Cost Note: Free plan is sufficient for one user.

Create or confirm statuses: Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Blocked, Review, Done.

Detailed Steps: Open project settings, inspect workflow/board columns, map statuses to columns.

Acceptance Criteria: Board columns match the study workflow.

Cost Note: No paid features required.

Add labels or components for setup, github, gcp, gcs, dataproc, spark, bigquery, airflow, qa, docs, cost.

Detailed Steps: Use project settings or import labels from the task sheet.

Acceptance Criteria: Imported work can be filtered by technology area.

Cost Note: No paid features required.

Save the Jira_Import sheet as CSV and use Jira external system import or issue import.

Detailed Steps: Map Summary, Issue Type, Description, Priority, Labels, Epic Link or Parent, Story Points, and Status fields.

Acceptance Criteria: Imported issues preserve task order and grouping.

Cost Note: Jira import behavior may vary by project type.

Add recurring personal calendar blocks for planning, build, review, and cleanup.

Detailed Steps: Pick 3-5 study windows per week and link them to Jira sprints or weekly board reviews.

Acceptance Criteria: Study cadence is visible and realistic.

Cost Note: No paid features required.

Summary: Check Git installation from VS Code terminal
Description:
Open VS Code terminal in this repo and run git --version, git status, and git branch.

Detailed Steps: Record output in notes if Git is missing or repo is not initialized.

Acceptance Criteria: Git works from the integrated terminal.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Run git config --global user.name and user.email with your GitHub identity.

Detailed Steps: Validate with git config --global --list.

Acceptance Criteria: Commits will show the correct author.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Install or validate GitHub CLI, then run gh auth login, or configure SSH keys for GitHub.

Detailed Steps: Use either HTTPS with gh auth or SSH; test with gh repo list or ssh -T git@github.com.

Acceptance Criteria: GitHub authentication works from VS Code terminal.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Create a new GitHub repository for your medallion learning work or push this folder as a branch/project.

Detailed Steps: Use GitHub UI or gh repo create, then add remote origin if needed.

Acceptance Criteria: Remote repo exists and local code can push.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Use main for stable notes and codex or feature branches for changes.

Detailed Steps: Create a first branch such as codex/jason-playground-plan and push it.

Acceptance Criteria: Branching workflow is ready for pull requests.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Install Python, Jupyter, Google Cloud Code, Remote SSH, GitHub Pull Requests, YAML, and optional Markdown extensions.

Detailed Steps: Use VS Code Extensions panel and verify each extension is enabled.

Acceptance Criteria: VS Code is ready for local, cloud, and remote work.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Inside JasonPlayground, create folders for datasets, src, dags, sql, notebooks, docs, and scripts.

Detailed Steps: Use terminal mkdir commands and commit the structure with placeholder README files if needed.

Acceptance Criteria: Folder layout supports medallion development.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Run pwd, dir, cd, mkdir, copy, move, rename, and remove-item on safe scratch files.

Detailed Steps: Keep the commands in docs/terminal_cheatsheet.md.

Acceptance Criteria: You can manage local files without leaving VS Code.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Sign in to Google Cloud and confirm billing/free trial status before creating resources.

Detailed Steps: Record account email, billing account name, and whether free credits are active in a private note outside git.

Acceptance Criteria: GCP account is ready and billing status is understood.

Cost Note: Budget alerts are still required.

Create a project such as jason-gcp-de-playground with a unique project id.

Detailed Steps: Use Console or gcloud projects create if organization policy allows it.

Acceptance Criteria: Dedicated learning project exists.

Cost Note: Project itself is not the main cost source.

Summary: Install and initialize Google Cloud CLI
Description:
Install gcloud, run gcloud init, login, and set the active project.

Detailed Steps: Validate with gcloud config list and gcloud projects describe PROJECT_ID.

Acceptance Criteria: gcloud works from VS Code terminal.

Cost Note: No direct cost.

Choose a low-cost region and set compute/Dataproc defaults.

Detailed Steps: Run gcloud config set compute/region and compute/zone.

Acceptance Criteria: Commands do not need region flags every time.

Cost Note: Region impacts price and availability.

Enable Compute Engine, Dataproc, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Cloud Composer, IAM, Secret Manager, and Cloud Logging APIs.

Detailed Steps: Use Console or gcloud services enable for each service.

Acceptance Criteria: All planned services can be created when needed.

Cost Note: Enabling APIs is generally free; resources are not.

Create a low monthly budget alert, for example USD 5 or 10, with notifications at 50, 80, and 100 percent.

Detailed Steps: Use Billing Budgets and Alerts in Console.

Acceptance Criteria: Cost alerts are active before creating compute resources.

Cost Note: Critical guardrail for free-trial use.

Create a service account for pipeline execution with least-privilege roles for storage, BigQuery, Dataproc, and Composer as needed.

Detailed Steps: Start narrow, then add roles only when a command fails due to missing permission.

Acceptance Criteria: Pipeline identity exists and keys are avoided unless truly needed.

Cost Note: No direct cost.

Create docs/cleanup_checklist.md covering Dataproc clusters, Composer environments, static IPs, buckets, BigQuery datasets, and budgets.

Detailed Steps: Add exact gcloud delete commands as you learn them.

Acceptance Criteria: Cleanup steps are ready before costly resources exist.

Cost Note: Prevents idle cloud spend.

Define tables for customers, products, orders, order_items, payments, shipments, inventory, stores, and clickstream events.

Detailed Steps: Write source-to-target notes and expected row counts in Dataset_Design sheet or docs.

Acceptance Criteria: Dataset design supports bronze, silver, and gold transformations.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Write a Python script that generates repeatable CSV and JSON files using a fixed seed.

Detailed Steps: Output small, medium, and optional large profiles.

Acceptance Criteria: Generated files can be recreated exactly.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Generate customers.csv, products.csv, stores.csv, orders.csv, order_items.csv, payments.csv, shipments.csv, and inventory.csv.

Detailed Steps: Use date-partition-friendly fields such as order_date and event_date.

Acceptance Criteria: CSV files exist with headers and realistic values.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Generate clickstream JSON lines and order_status_event JSON lines with nested fields.

Detailed Steps: Include event_id, event_ts, user/session ids, and payload attributes.

Acceptance Criteria: JSON files exercise semi-structured ingestion.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Define expected row counts, unique keys, allowed statuses, required columns, and referential integrity checks.

Detailed Steps: Store expectations in docs/data_quality_rules.md or a YAML file.

Acceptance Criteria: Each dataset has at least three validation rules.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Choose globally unique bucket names for bronze, silver, gold, scripts, and temp or use one bucket with prefixes.

Detailed Steps: Record naming convention and region in docs/gcp_objects.md.

Acceptance Criteria: Bucket plan is clear before creation.

Cost Note: Bucket storage costs are small but real.

Use gcloud storage buckets create or Console to create the project bucket in your chosen region.

Detailed Steps: Enable uniform bucket-level access unless a lesson requires object ACLs.

Acceptance Criteria: Bucket exists and is visible from CLI.

Cost Note: Storage charges apply by volume.

Create prefixes such as bronze/csv/orders/load_date=YYYY-MM-DD and bronze/json/clickstream/load_date=YYYY-MM-DD.

Detailed Steps: Use local path mirrors before uploading.

Acceptance Criteria: Bronze structure follows medallion raw-zone convention.

Cost Note: No meaningful cost beyond storage.

Use gcloud storage cp or gsutil cp to upload generated CSV files to bronze paths.

Detailed Steps: Validate with gcloud storage ls and compare local file counts.

Acceptance Criteria: CSV files are in GCS bronze.

Cost Note: Storage and operation charges apply.

Upload generated JSON files to bronze/json paths and validate object names.

Detailed Steps: Use recursive commands and avoid overwriting unrelated paths.

Acceptance Criteria: JSON files are in GCS bronze.

Cost Note: Storage and operation charges apply.

Generate a manifest with source file name, path, row count, checksum, format, and load timestamp.

Detailed Steps: Store manifest locally and in GCS bronze/manifests.

Acceptance Criteria: Bronze files are auditable.

Cost Note: No major cost.

Create a short-lived single-node cluster with component gateway enabled and optional JupyterLab if desired.

Detailed Steps: Use small machine types and labels such as purpose=learning owner=jason.

Acceptance Criteria: Cluster starts successfully.

Cost Note: Delete when idle; compute costs can grow quickly.

Run gcloud compute ssh to connect to the Dataproc master node.

Detailed Steps: Exit and reconnect until the workflow is comfortable.

Acceptance Criteria: SSH works from VS Code terminal.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Summary: Connect VS Code Remote SSH to Dataproc
Description:
Configure Remote SSH target using gcloud-generated SSH config or direct host settings.

Detailed Steps: Open a remote VS Code window on the Dataproc node.

Acceptance Criteria: VS Code can edit files on the cluster.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Clone the GitHub repository on the cluster and checkout the working branch.

Detailed Steps: Validate git status and project files on the remote host.

Acceptance Criteria: Remote cluster has project code.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Run spark-sql --version and pyspark, then read a small bronze file from GCS.

Detailed Steps: Confirm Spark can access GCS without manual credential files.

Acceptance Criteria: Spark can read the raw lake path.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Summary: Open Spark UI through component gateway
Description:
Find the Dataproc web interfaces and open Spark History Server or Spark UI.

Detailed Steps: Run a sample job and locate it in the UI.

Acceptance Criteria: You can inspect job stages and logs.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Create Spark logic to read CSV and JSON bronze files with explicit schemas.

Detailed Steps: Avoid inferSchema for production-style code; put schemas in code or config.

Acceptance Criteria: Spark reads all source datasets with expected data types.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Clean customer names, emails, dates, geography fields, and deduplicate by customer_id.

Detailed Steps: Write Parquet partitioned by load_date or customer_region if useful.

Acceptance Criteria: silver/customers path is clean and queryable.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Standardize product categories, prices, active flags, and effective dates.

Detailed Steps: Validate product_id uniqueness and nonnegative prices.

Acceptance Criteria: silver/products path is clean and queryable.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Normalize order timestamps, statuses, customer references, and order dates.

Detailed Steps: Partition by order_date and reject invalid statuses into a quarantine path.

Acceptance Criteria: silver/orders path is clean and partitioned.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Validate item quantities, subtotal calculations, and product references.

Detailed Steps: Recalculate subtotal and flag mismatches for review.

Acceptance Criteria: silver/order_items path is clean and validated.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Standardize payment methods, amounts, payment status, and timestamps.

Detailed Steps: Validate no successful negative payments unless intentionally generated as refunds.

Acceptance Criteria: silver/payments path is clean and typed.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Normalize carrier, tracking status, shipped_at, delivered_at, and delivery duration.

Detailed Steps: Flag impossible delivery dates into quarantine.

Acceptance Criteria: silver/shipments path is clean and typed.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Flatten JSON event payloads and standardize event timestamps, event names, session ids, and device fields.

Detailed Steps: Partition by event_date.

Acceptance Criteria: silver/clickstream path is clean and partitioned.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running for validation.

Create a parameterized PySpark job with arguments for source path, target path, run date, and environment.

Detailed Steps: Run it locally on Dataproc using spark-submit.

Acceptance Criteria: Job can run one dataset at a time using parameters.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Summary: Submit silver job through Dataproc Jobs
Description:
Use gcloud dataproc jobs submit pyspark with parameters for each silver dataset.

Detailed Steps: Record job ids and logs.

Acceptance Criteria: Silver transformations run as managed Dataproc jobs.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Use gcloud storage ls, spark-sql, and PySpark count checks to confirm output paths, partitions, row counts, and schema.

Detailed Steps: Compare against data quality expectations.

Acceptance Criteria: Silver layer passes checks.

Cost Note: Cluster must be running.

Create datasets such as bronze_meta, silver_external, and gold_marts or a clean equivalent naming convention.

Detailed Steps: Set region to match GCS/Dataproc where possible.

Acceptance Criteria: BigQuery datasets exist.

Cost Note: BigQuery storage/query charges may apply.

Summary: Create external tables over silver Parquet
Description:
Create BigQuery external tables or BigLake-style references for silver Parquet paths.

Detailed Steps: Validate schema and partition pruning where available.

Acceptance Criteria: BigQuery can query silver data.

Cost Note: Query costs may apply.

Define dim_customer, dim_product, dim_store, dim_date, fact_order_item, fact_payment, fact_shipment, and aggregate marts.

Detailed Steps: Document grain and primary keys for each table.

Acceptance Criteria: Gold model has clear grain and relationships.

Cost Note: No major cost until data is materialized/queried.

Use BigQuery SQL or Spark to populate customer, product, store, and date dimensions.

Detailed Steps: Include surrogate-key strategy or document why natural keys are acceptable for learning.

Acceptance Criteria: Dimension tables are queryable and documented.

Cost Note: Query/storage costs apply.

Create fact_order_item, fact_payment, and fact_shipment from silver tables.

Detailed Steps: Validate joins and amounts.

Acceptance Criteria: Fact tables are at documented grain.

Cost Note: Query/storage costs apply.

Aggregate revenue, order count, item count, customer count, and average order value by date, product, and store.

Detailed Steps: Compare totals to silver source data.

Acceptance Criteria: daily_sales_mart is ready for analysis.

Cost Note: Query/storage costs apply.

Aggregate shipped, delivered, delayed, and average delivery duration by carrier and date.

Detailed Steps: Validate delayed shipment logic.

Acceptance Criteria: fulfillment_mart is ready for analysis.

Cost Note: Query/storage costs apply.

Join sales and clickstream activity by customer/date where generated data supports it.

Detailed Steps: Calculate sessions, product views, purchases, and conversion rate.

Acceptance Criteria: customer_behavior_mart is ready for analysis.

Cost Note: Query/storage costs apply.

Write SQL checks for row counts, revenue reconciliation, null primary keys, duplicate keys, and invalid date ranges.

Detailed Steps: Store checks in sql/validation.

Acceptance Criteria: Gold layer has repeatable validation queries.

Cost Note: Query costs apply.

Summary: Create analysis notebook or saved queries
Description:
Create a small notebook or saved SQL file showing top products, revenue trends, and fulfillment performance.

Detailed Steps: Use only gold tables.

Acceptance Criteria: You can explain the business outputs of the pipeline.

Cost Note: Query costs apply.

Create a small Composer environment only when ready to orchestrate and delete it after the module if cost is a concern.

Detailed Steps: Record environment name, region, bucket, and Airflow UI URL.

Acceptance Criteria: Composer environment is available.

Cost Note: Composer can be costly; use carefully.

Create dags folder and install or document compatible Airflow provider versions for local linting if needed.

Detailed Steps: Keep DAG code independent of hard-coded project ids where possible.

Acceptance Criteria: DAG source folder is ready.

Cost Note: Local setup no GCP cost.

Define variables for project_id, region, bucket, dataproc_cluster, run_date, bronze_prefix, silver_prefix, and gold_dataset.

Detailed Steps: Create them in Airflow UI or via gcloud composer environments run.

Acceptance Criteria: DAG config is externalized.

Cost Note: No major extra cost.

Create DAG with logical task groups: precheck, bronze_validation, silver_processing, gold_processing, validation, notify_or_log.

Detailed Steps: Use clear task ids and dependencies.

Acceptance Criteria: DAG parses in Airflow UI.

Cost Note: Composer must be running.

Add BashOperator or PythonOperator tasks to check GCS object existence and manifest freshness.

Detailed Steps: Fail fast if required source files are missing.

Acceptance Criteria: Pipeline stops before Spark if bronze is incomplete.

Cost Note: Composer must be running.

Use Dataproc job operators or gcloud command tasks to submit silver PySpark jobs.

Detailed Steps: Pass dataset-specific arguments and run date.

Acceptance Criteria: Airflow can trigger silver Spark jobs.

Cost Note: Composer and Dataproc cost apply.

Use BigQueryInsertJobOperator or bq commands to run gold SQL scripts in dependency order.

Detailed Steps: Parameterize project and dataset names.

Acceptance Criteria: Airflow can build gold tables.

Cost Note: Query costs apply.

Copy DAG file to the Composer environment dags bucket using gcloud storage cp or gsutil cp.

Detailed Steps: Watch Airflow UI for import errors.

Acceptance Criteria: DAG appears without parse errors.

Cost Note: Composer must be running.

Trigger the DAG manually and monitor each task in Airflow UI.

Detailed Steps: Capture failed logs, fix config, and rerun as needed.

Acceptance Criteria: End-to-end DAG succeeds once.

Cost Note: Composer and Dataproc cost apply.

Set retries, retry delays, task-level timeouts, and failure logging.

Detailed Steps: Keep alerts simple for solo learning, such as Airflow logs and email if configured.

Acceptance Criteria: DAG has realistic operational controls.

Cost Note: No major extra cost.

Document the medallion architecture, GCS paths, Dataproc jobs, BigQuery datasets, and Airflow DAG.

Detailed Steps: Include a simple text diagram or Mermaid diagram.

Acceptance Criteria: A future reader can understand the project.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Maintain docs/terminal_journal.md with commands used for Git, Windows files, gcloud, GCS, Dataproc SSH, and Composer.

Detailed Steps: Group commands by module and explain placeholders.

Acceptance Criteria: You have a reusable command reference.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Track errors, root cause, fix, and prevention notes from setup through orchestration.

Detailed Steps: Add at least one entry per module.

Acceptance Criteria: You build debugging memory as part of the project.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Create scripts that run local schema checks and SQL validation checks where practical.

Detailed Steps: Use simple CLI commands that can be repeated.

Acceptance Criteria: Core checks are not only manual.

Cost Note: Minimal local cost.

Open a PR from the learning branch to main with a checklist and summary of completed modules.

Detailed Steps: Review changes before merging.

Acceptance Criteria: You practice professional code review flow.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.

Delete Composer environment, Dataproc cluster, static IPs, unused buckets, temporary BigQuery tables, and any service-account keys.

Detailed Steps: Confirm billing dashboard after cleanup.

Acceptance Criteria: No idle costly resources remain.

Cost Note: Most important cost-control step.

Map completed work to skills: Git, VS Code, GCS, Dataproc, Spark, BigQuery, Composer, data modeling, QA, and operations.

Detailed Steps: Update Jira statuses and write a short retrospective.

Acceptance Criteria: Project is ready for next iteration or portfolio polish.

Cost Note: No GCP cost.
